brief.headline: Push for longer payment terms — they take 105 days to pay their own suppliers, so asking them to wait 45 days for our payment is only fair.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match maker pricing — they are a pure trader (100% traded goods), so our price carries their reseller margin.
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume, in line with market headroom
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc), with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec. Since they manufacture nothing (100.0% traded), their price includes a reseller margin — benchmark to a maker's rate to strip that out.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 45 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹5.36 L for us if we move to 30-day standard; an extra 15 days beyond that frees another ₹2.68 L.

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.8% as profit on every ₹100 they sell — very thin — so a hard price squeeze could break them. But they already take 105 days to pay their own suppliers (vs 57 days for similar firms), meaning they stretch payment themselves. We are 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr in sales — a solid chunk — so we have the weight to ask for better terms. Their money-health score is weak (2/10) and they sit in the grey distress zone (1.58), so keep the ask focused on terms and a fair traded-vs-maker price gap, not a brutal cut that tips them over.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Health score B (65/100), revenue ₹2569.83 Cr — a robust second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (market backup)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer, pan-India, medium confidence.

risks: Their money-health is weak (2/10) and they sit in the grey distress zone (1.58) — a supply-continuity risk. Do not load too much volume through them; qualify a second source now.
Pending legal case(s) flagged — ask for details and assess any risk to their ability to deliver.
They manufacture nothing (100.0% traded) — they are a middleman, so any maker squeeze upstream flows straight to us. Lock in a direct-maker alternate.
Profit is only 2.8% — if we push price too hard, they may stop supplying or cut corners. Win on payment terms and the trader-vs-maker gap, not a brutal cut.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You take 105 days to pay your suppliers — we'd like to move to 45 days on our side, and since you're reselling (not making) this packaging, let's talk about closing the gap to a maker's price at higher volume.
